subject: ENGLISH
title: Picture Detective · M01 D01
objective: Describe people, places, objects, and actions using evidence from a picture.
introduction: Milo is a picture detective today! Look at the picture and name only what you can really see.

vocabulary.definition: A group of words that tells a complete idea.
An image that shows details you can look at and describe.
A person who looks for clues to find the answer.

activities.instruction: Watch how detectives name what they see in a picture!
activities.content: A good description names what is visible and uses a complete sentence.

feedback.retry: Check the picture: name only a visible detail in a complete sentence. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: A good description names what is visible and uses a complete sentence.

activities.instruction: Tap each example and read what you can see!

examples: The child holds a red kite.
Two birds sit in the tree.
A dog runs beside the bench.

feedback.correct: Great! You found the examples for Picture Detective. 🔎
feedback.retry: Tap a detail you can see, then read the sentence that names it. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A numbered list of the same examples is available for keyboard and screen-reader use.

activities.instruction: Sort each card: is it something the picture shows?

fits: The child holds a red kite.
Two birds sit in the tree.
A dog runs beside the bench.
doesNotFit: Guessing what is outside the picture
Naming a color that is not shown

feedback.correct: Great! You sorted the examples using the Picture Detective clue. 🎉
feedback.retry: Sort by picture evidence: keep visible details apart from guesses and fragments. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Tap an item and then tap a labeled category; dragging is optional.

feedback.retry: Trace the kite string to the hand holding it. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: All choices are visible text and selectable with TalkBack.

activities.instruction: Match each sentence to who or what it is about!

pairs.left: The child holds a red kite.
Two birds sit in the tree.
A dog runs beside the bench.

feedback.correct: Great! You matched each example with its Picture Detective explanation. 🔗
feedback.retry: Match each sentence with the person or animal named in it. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A list-based matching control replaces drag gestures.

activities.instruction: Put the steps for describing a picture in order!

steps: Name what you see in a complete sentence.
Check that your sentence uses evidence from the picture.

feedback.correct: Great! You put the Picture Detective steps in order. 🎉
feedback.retry: Order the process: look, name a visible detail, then check the evidence. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Up and down buttons provide an alternative to dragging.

items.prompt: Which one is a complete sentence about the picture?

options.text: Under the big tree
The child holds a red kite.
A red kite
The red kite

items.explanation: “The child holds a red kite.” names who does something, so it is a complete sentence. The other choices are only pieces of a sentence.

items.prompt: Which detail can you see in the picture?

options.text: A puppy sleeps in a basket.
Rain falls on the bench.
The child holds a red kite.
A yellow bus passes the school.

items.explanation: The child with the red kite is in the picture, so you can see it. The puppy and the rain are not shown, so name only what is visible.

items.prompt: Which is NOT something you can see in the picture?

options.text: A dog runs beside the bench.
A tiger sleeps in the school.
Two birds sit in the tree.
The child holds a red kite.

items.explanation: Two birds and a dog are in the picture, but there is no tiger in school. A good description names only what the picture really shows.

options.text: The child
The tree
The dog
The birds

items.explanation: The kite string is in the child's hand, so the child is holding the kite. Dogs and trees cannot hold a kite.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes the picture using evidence?

options.text: The kite is green.
The child feels sad today.
A dog runs beside the bench.
The child is thinking about tomorrow.

items.explanation: “A dog runs beside the bench.” uses a detail you can see. The kite is red, not green, and feelings like sadness are not visible in the picture.

assetSpecs.prompt: Friendly Grade 3 cartoon storybook concept board for Picture Detective; rounded shapes, warm dark-brown outlines, tropical palette, no embedded text, uncluttered small-screen layout. Compose overlays provide labels and interactive targets.
assetSpecs.contentDescription: Five connected learning tokens for exploring examples in Picture Detective.
